items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: we’d start the second half with Duke Ellington and I would do the Ivy Anderson.

ctx.x: Yeah. And we laugh a little bit about that you know. But we know where we’re going and what we’re going to do, and we like to think of music as being theatre. When Bob was director of the Smithsonian, we put on a theatrical performance. It began with me singing a cappella “Back Water Blues,” and then went into “Mournful Serenade.” On a darkened stage, Bob would walk out onto a darkened stage and talk about what is jazz, and then would build. And we would do an hour and a half of the whole history of jazz,…

would go on to Thelonious Monk, Charlie Parker, Dizzy Gillespie, and I would sing something attributed to Sarah Vaughan in her younger days, and close up with I think Count Basie’s “Jumpin’ at the Woodside.” And it was a whole history of jazz. But we presented it as theater. I would wear clothes that depicted the era with Eva Taylor, as Eva would have dressed, and as the stylistic way of Ivy Anderson, who was very elegant, and the way that Sarah Vaughan dressed. I mean it was all theater. We mustn’t forget that.…
